reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of the paper is that causal inference in sports analytics must begin with precise estimand definition—whether average treatment effect (ATE), treatment effect on the treated (ATT), or treatment effect on the non-treated (ATNT). These estimands are mathematically grounded in potential outcomes theory, where each unit has two potential outcomes under treatment and control. The framework requires explicit assumptions such as consistency, positivity (overlap), no interference (SUTVA), and no unmeasured confounding. In practice, these translate into data requirements: sufficient variation in treatment assignment conditional on confounders, and valid observational data that reflects the causal structure. The paper demonstrates this using a soccer dataset where crossing attempts are treated as interventions affecting shot creation. Propensity score matching ensures balance across confounders, and dual standard errors provide robust inference. This protocol enables GSE to build causal models that can reason about counterfactuals and support strategic decision-making.
